Native SAS build and Stata fits used all 14 current local files listed above. Aggregate handoffs contain 109,055 Table 2 and 81,473 Table 3 firm-quarters, both through DATADATE 2002-12-31; source/final coverage is evidenced by work/runtime/20261118T082501166776Z/build.lst pp.26–27, work/data/table2_valuation/reg.dta, and work/data/table3_information/reg.dta.
changes: Extended inclusive calendar DATADATE/PENDS/FPEDATS bounds from 1989–1997 to 1989–2002; retained the original 1989 start and pooled all years in each model.

Shifted dependent-source upper limits for daily/monthly exchange rates, monthly security descriptors/prices, AJEXDI factors, and CRSP market sessions from 1999-12-31 to 2004-12-31; kept all role-date price selection, t−3/t+3 lags, RDQ matching, three-session event definition, model terms, and pooled OLS estimator unchanged.

Added a per-calendar-year Compustat GVKEY/DATADATE duplicate-key audit and per-fit diagnostics counted on active Stata e(sample), with lowercase DATADATE retained and counted as SAS/ Stata day units since 1960-01-01.
limitations: The paper says its 1989–1997 sample ends because it requires primary EPS and most I/B/E/S data are fully diluted from 1998 (physical p.2). Current IBES.ACTU_EPSUS contains qualifying EPS/QTR/US-firm actual records in 1998–2002, but its field inventory has no basic/primary-versus-diluted actual-basis indicator. The extension therefore replays the accepted ACTU approximation through 2002; it is not verified as a basic/primary-only sample and should be read as a conditional temporal extension.

The current replay’s Table 2 1989–1997 e(sample) has 48,307 rows, one more than the accepted saved fit’s N=48,306; Table 3 is 33,602 in both. Available aggregate evidence does not identify the source of the single-row Table 2 difference.

The accepted reconstruction already differed from published sample sizes: its Table 2 and Table 3 fits used N=48,306 and N=33,602 versus published N=22,024 and N=22,092. The extended pooled fits use N=109,055 and N=81,473, respectively. These sample-size and coefficient comparisons do not remove the construction’s prior best-effort assumptions, including same-IID share-basis support, the undocumented price timing, and the CRSP value-weighted benchmark.

The longer Compustat window has 525 nonunique GVKEY/DATADATE keys after descriptor screens; the accepted q_unique rule excludes those keys rather than resolving ties. Duplicate-key counts for 1998–2002 are 44, 27, 39, 46, and 29. Final Table 2 and Table 3 handoffs have unique firm-quarter keys. The Table 3 construction also excluded 870 incomplete event windows under the accepted complete three-session return rule.

The four assigned scopes are the accepted full-sample baseline fits only. Predictive-ability tests, group-specific table columns, the 63-day information window, and paired coefficient/Vuong tests remain outside the assigned predecessor scopes; no paired statistics were inferred from separate regressions.
